#4245. The Switch 2 Pro Controller Can Make Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Even Better

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time hit Switch 2 today, and, as Kyle Hilliard pointed out in our review, it is pretty excellent. Along with its remarkable visual upgrade, the new Switch 2 remake of Ocarina of Time adds quality-of-life improvements and modernizes the control scheme. As part of that, Nintendo has added the ability to jump and sprint. While that works well to make the game feel new, I quickly realized it sometimes clashes with another new improvement: a free camera controlled by the right stick. Holding down the sprint button to get through areas as fast as possible can make it tricky to keep the camera where you want it, but thankfully, if you have the Switch 2 Pro Controller, there's an easy fix.

After hours of running around, I was awestruck by the level of detail and updates, but I found myself constantly fighting with the camera, or at the very least, needing to take a strange claw-style grip to be able to direct the camera with the right stick, while holding down the A button to sprint. If you're a casual Switch 2 player, you might not have even noticed the back buttons on the Pro Controller, or you just have no idea what they do. Those buttons can be remapped on a per-game basis and it's a simple process. Everyone has their own preferences, but, for example, for high-mobility shooters, I like remapping one of those to reload and one to jump. I've never felt the need to remap in a Zelda game, but after feeling the need to do so with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2, I might do so going forward.

If you, like me, struggle to comfortably steer the new free camera while running through hallways, towns, dungeons, and, yes, Hyrule Field, you might want to consider remapping your controller. As you can see in the above image, the placement of Jump and Dash on the face buttons can make it difficult to simultaneously control the camera and sprint. This isn't typically a problem in most modern games, as clicking the right stick is often a toggle to sprint, but in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Switch 2, you need to hold the button.

If you have the Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller, copying one button's functionality to the buttons on the back of the controller is simple. All you need to do is hold the Home button on the Switch 2 Pro Controller for a moment until the Switch 2 system menu appears on the right side. Along with Power Options and any Bluetooth audio devices you have available, there is also the option to map GL and GR, the controller's back buttons on the left and right, respectively.

Navigate down the menu to the GL and GR, then select which one you'd like to map. It will ask you which button you want to assign to the one you selected. Everyone can choose whatever makes sense in their own head, but mapping A (Roll and Dash) to GL and X (Jump) to GR made the most sense to me. Now, while I'm using the Switch 2 Pro Controller, I can use my middle finger to hold the GL button to Dash around without removing my thumb from the camera-controlling right stick.

And the best part is that, since you're not removing the functionality of the A or X buttons, you can still use them when it makes sense. For example, A also controls actions like opening up a treasure chest or door, and in my head, that feels like a face-button action, whereas rolling and dashing feel right mapped to the back buttons. The only downside is that, since this functionality is new for Switch 2 Pro Controllers, it isn't available if you're using the Joy-Cons or a Switch 1 Pro Controller. Also, it can make switching over to handheld mode challenging, as you don't have access to the back buttons in that play style.

Even if you don't have the ability to take advantage of this tip, either because you don't own a Switch 2 Pro Controller or because you prefer playing in handheld mode, you should still absolutely play the Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. To learn more about the experience and why it's a must-play, head to our review.

#4244. Godzilla Minus Zero ending explained: what happens to Ghidorah, who dies, and does it set up a sequel?

Everything you need to know about the Godzilla Minus Zero ending explained

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The Godzilla Minus Zero ending is a dramatic one, with tons of kaiju action. So, you'd be forgiven on missing some of the finer details of what exactly goes down at the conclusion.

That's where we come in. Below, we've got a summary of the film's ending as well as a breakdown of all the biggest questions, so you can get up to speed at a glance. Naturally, that means there are spoilers ahead for the film. Turn back now if you're not up to date!

So, for everything you need to know about the Godzilla Minus Zero ending, head to the below. For even more on the film, check out our spoiler-free Godzilla Minus Zero review.

The Godzilla Minus Zero ending kicks off with a plan to bring Ghidorah and Godzilla to the same place in Ginza, Tokyo and have them fight. Ghidorah is lured to the location with generators, since the kaiju loves electricity, while Godzilla is lured there via a resonance wave machine made by biologist Kanji Murakami – the frequency attracts the kaiju when Noriko Shikishima is hooked up to it, since Noriko has Godzilla's DNA embedded in her after being attacked in the first film.

Godzilla and Ghidorah do indeed start fighting once they see each other, but Ghidorah is able to overpower Godzilla. The plan is to trap Ghidorah and freeze him with liquid nitrogen, but, when the trap is threatened by the destruction, Kenji Noda goes to fix the fuel lines himself – and his car is caught in a blast from Ghidorah. Noda is trapped, but Koichi Shikishima fires a missile from his plane to attack Ghidorah, accidentally killing Noda in the process. However, meteorologist Makoto Aoyama lies to him that Ghidorah was the one who killed Noda, sparing Koichi any further guilt.

Godzilla is then revived with the resonance machine, and both kaijus gear up for another showdown. This time, though, Godzilla is able to kill Ghidorah with his atomic ray. The US military then arrive on the scene and begin to attack Godzilla, before they are given orders to stand down.

Koichi holds Murakami at gunpoint, planning to escape with Noriko, before it's revealed that Murakami is on their side. Together, they destroy the plane and the resonance wave machine: Murakami has already set a trap to destroy his own research. This way, no one will be able to control Godzilla or use Noriko and her Godzilla DNA in the future, ending the cycle of war.

Godzilla returns to the ocean, but Murakami is captured by the US military before he can escape. Koichi and Noriko plan to go on the run and leave their child, Akiko, behind for her safety, but cannot bring themselves to abandon her. They end the film escaping together as a family.

Countless civilians die in Godzilla Minus Zero, but there is only one major character death. Hidetaka Yoshioka's Kenji Noda dies in the showdown with Ghidorah, when Ghidorah's energy blast crashes Noda's car and traps him. Koichi then fires a missile from his plane, which inadvertently kills Noda in the ensuing explosion – though, meteorologist Makoto Aoyama lies to him that Ghidorah was responsible for Noda's death to spare him further guilt.

No, New York City is not really attacked in Godzilla Minus Zero. This is a dream sequence from Min Tanaka's Kanji Murakami, who lost his family in the atomic bombing of Hiroshima. He secretly harbors a desire for revenge and wishes to unleash Godzilla on New York City to inflict the same kind of damage – though he is ultimately convinced against his plan by Kenji Noda.

Ghidorah takes a lot of damage in the film, but it's Godzilla who finally finishes him off. After Godzilla is seriously hurt by Ghidorah, he is able to regenerate and return for another round after Noriko and the team on the plane wake him with the resonance machine. He charges up his atomic breath and, this time, is finally able to kill Ghidorah.

After winning his battle with Ghidorah, Godzilla simply returns to the sea. It seems the US military had designs on controlling the kaiju with the resonance wave machine, though luckily it gets destroyed before anyone can get their hands on it. That means Godzilla is free – though that probably means he's likely to continue his rampages, which could be bad news for Tokyo.

This is a resonance wave machine, which is capable of attracting Godzilla thanks to the kaiju's DNA Noriko still carries in her body after being attacked in the previous film. The machine is used to lure Godzilla to the site of the showdown with Ghidorah, though, when the US military arrives, everyone onboard the ship makes the decision to destroy the machine and everything in the plane so it cannot be used to control Godzilla's movements in the future and continue the cycle of war. All of Kanji Murakami's research is also destroyed.

The US military wants to use the resonance wave machine so that they can control Godzilla's movements (though, this wouldn't control Godzilla entirely, it would just make it possible to lure him somewhere). It's heavily implied that the US desires Godzilla and his atomic breath as a weapon when troops are ordered not to hurt the kaiju.

No, Koichi and Noriko do not leave Akiko behind. In the end, they don't have the heart to after Akiko gets extremely upset at the idea of them abandoning her. Of course, the young couple think they're doing the right thing, since they're likely to be on the run forever thanks to Noriko's Godzilla DNA and Koichi's role in helping to destroy the resonance wave machine. Still, Akiko is probably better off with her parents than without them, so it's a welcome sight to see the youngster on the motorbike with Koichi and Noriko at the end.

Godzilla Minus Zero certainly leaves the door open for a third film, though nothing has been confirmed yet. Koichi and Noriko are on the run with Akiko, and Godzilla escaped into the ocean, while Kanji Murakami is in the custody of the US military. These are all plot threads that could be picked up in a third film.

"I have been a huge Godzilla fan since I was a small child, and I swung for the fences with Godzilla Minus Zero," director Takashi Yamazaki recently told SFX magazine. "[These films] are huge milestones, looking back at my career and in my life so far. But that doesn't mean I would never work on another Godzilla film again. If Toho came to me with another offer to explore this world even further, I'd probably say yes.

"Yet at the same time, if you told me this is my last Godzilla film, I would be quite satisfied with what we were able to achieve," he continued. "I'm very grateful to Toho for trusting me with their baby. I'm just happy that I was a Godzilla fan, because that's what enabled me to do this." So, we'll just have to wait and see.

Godzilla Minus Zero is in theaters now. For more, check out our guide to all the most exciting upcoming movies left of 2026.

#4243. Zenless Zone Zero Version 2.8 is refreshing your team comps with a new mechanic, and the game is coming to Steam

Zenless Zone Zero will soon become the first HoYoverse game to make its way to Steam, though we wish we had more details.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a pretty exciting Zenless Zone Zero Special Program that not only delivered all the details on the next big update, it also came with the unexpected announcement that the action RPG is on its way to Steam.

Previously, all HoYoverse games with PC versions have always been directly available from the developer’s website, or through the Epic Games Store. In other words, Zenless Zone Zero will soon mark the massive company’s debut on Valve’s platform.

The main focus of the livestream, of course, has been Version 2.8, otherwise known as New Eridan Sunset. This upcoming release is scheduled for May 6, though the Steam version does not yet have a date.The new release sees the release of two new Agents, as well as the brand-new Wind attribute enemy.

The release also acts as the last chapter of Season 2, and it sees Ramiel becoming the main target of different factions in the Outer Ring. The two new arrivals, together with Proxies and Cissia will embark on a quest to learn the new identity of Ramiel.

The first new Agent is Promeia, the executioner of Krampus. She’s an S-Rank Ice Anomaly Agent who can consume Trial by Cold to trigger Abloom on enemies. This is done by converting Corrosive Chill.

By using her EX Special Attack, she can enter the Bound Absolution state, which allows her to automatically Perfect Dodge any attack that targets her. If you have another Anomaly or Support Agent on the team, Promeia can further boost the entire squad’s Abloom damage.

The second addition in 2.8 is Starlight - Billy, also an S-Rank Agent, though wielding Physical Rupture instead. This is the upgraded form of Billy, and he arrives on a combat motorcycle to bring his signature Starlight Knight to the fight. Through it, he can deliver big Physical burst damage.

The higher Billy’s health, the more Sheer damage he deals. In fact, all Physical damage he deals lands as Sheer damage. Further building on his tank-like role, his skills can also restore his own health.

Re-runs in Version 2.8 will be Lucia in the first half, and Orphie & Magus in the second. The other exciting addition coming with this update is the new Wind attribute enemy, and the accompanying Vortex mechanic.

When an enemy is inflicted with the Wind Attribute Anomaly, any other Anomaly attack type that gets applied will trigger Vortex, rather than Disorder. This deals AoE Anomaly damage of the type that matches the corresponding element.

Throughout the version’s runtime, you’ll be able to take part in the Marcel Bootopia-themed event, which gives you control of Eous and lets you explore a Bangboo resort island. The island has been closed due to an outbreak of Hollows, and you must rescue Bangboos and find treasures.

If you do, you’ll earn Booltergeist and its Bangboo core for your troubles. This is an A-Rank Bangboo that can float around and fire lasers in combat. Its damage is further boosted whenever certain teammates are present.

The Ultimate Verdict Trial is another event you can check out that lets you fight alongside newcomer Promeia, or take part in other mini-activities that all reward Polychrome. Finally, you can look forward to a new Hoshimi Miyabi outfit: Dignified Blossom, which will be available in the store.

Before you jump back in next month, it always helps to catch up on the latest Zenless Zone Zero codes to make sure you’re not missing out on any freebies.

#4242. Feature: "I Will Have Been Here For 30 Hours" - London's Midnight Zelda Launch Was Wild

"When it gets to midnight, I will have been here for 30 hours."

That's what Sinaa, one of the people right at the very front of the queue for Zelda: Ocarina of Time's London midnight launch, told me last night.

They had camped out from 6pm the night before, sleeping underneath two chairs outside the Tottenham Court Road Argos, all to ensure they got their hands on the game (and its special N64-inspired casing) as soon as possible.

To my shame, I had underestimated the event a little. With just 48 hours' notice, I assumed that it might not be quite so grand an affair, perhaps pulling in 100 or so die-hard fans and little more. This is a Nintendo pop-up in an Argos we're talking about, not a flagship Nintendo Store.

I arrived just before 9pm and the queue was already around the block. Literally. Extending from the camping chairs at the very front of the line, those of us eager to get our hands on the game lined up around the entire circumference of the central London store. At one point, the line was so long that its end stood right next to its beginning, like a cruel game of Snake.

The people waiting were anything but cruel, though. Walking its length, I spoke to fans who had travelled in from other cities for this event alone.

Some were dressed up. One kept everyone entertained with tunes on an Ocarina. One person's mum held down the fort at the front of the line, pretending to be an Argos employee to deter anyone from cutting in at the eleventh hour. There were full Switch Sports Resort tournaments going on at one point.

Everyone was very welcoming, very friendly, and very excited to get their hands on Ocarina of Time again. I asked which moment people were the most hyped to revisit and heard everything from "the title screen" to "the bottom of the well", "Kokiri Village" to "bopping Ganondorf".

For most of us, this was a long-awaited homecoming. A few of the people I spoke to were about to experience the game for the first time, but the vast majority already had multiple N64 playthroughs under their belts. (A particular shoutout to the one person whose formative memories of the game came from playing the demo in Smash Bros. Brawl.) If anything was going to encourage people to double- or triple-dip, it was Ocarina.

There was a fair amount of confusion from those who weren't in the know, naturally. As the doors opened and the queue began to crawl to the entrance, people shouted their "What are you all queuing for?" confusion across the street. Multiple cars stopped and wound down windows to ask the same question.

It really became a test of spirit when the clock slipped past 2am, and those of us who had arrived that evening were yet to make it to the front of the store. A little early-morning argy-bargy ensued among a few people behind us when one accused the other of pushing in. A short-lived altercation, to be sure, and likely a product of 5+ hours on our feet without the end of the line in sight.

After edging towards the front of the line, we were finally in. Let me say right now, the Argos staff were wonderful. Even at 2am, the person serving me was still happy enough to talk about the night, the game, and even very kindly laugh along with me when I jokingly said I had "just popped into the store to pick up something else, actually" (it was very late, and I am very sorry).

The copy itself? Sublime. Sure, the cardboard on the N64-inspired box doesn't boast quite the same flimsiness as we had back in the '90s, but it's a real looker, nonetheless.

The foil cover is a treat for the eyes, too — I wasn't expecting to get that one, so it was a nice surprise — and hey, why not add another Zelda keyring to the collection?

I'm sure that some people will have left the event empty-handed. Argos informed me that they only had 500 copies of the game, and the queue far exceeded that number. Nintendo UK says that over 600 people were there last night, but at one point, I would have easily stuck an extra hundred on top of that estimate.

I left very sleepy, with very sore feet. But I also left with a very full heart, and a new copy of one of my favourite games of all time. I hope all of those NL readers I met there had an equally wonderful time, and hopefully the sleep deprivation isn't enough to distract from some OoT-ing later on today.

Now, if you'll excuse me, I need to pour my fifth cup of coffee.

#4240. Genshin Impact Luna 7 brings us the first playable Hexenzirkel as things take a turn in Sumeru

Genshin Impact's Luna 7 update will kick off a new Archon Quest chapter, and deliver some interesting new additions to the playable roster.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a new Genshin Impact Special Program, where the developer revealed everything there is to know about the game’s next major update. Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana, or as its friends call it, Luna 7, was unveiled as part of the showcase.

This next update has a lot going for it, and it will be in players’ hands everywhere on May 20.

Luna 7 will take us back to Sumeru for its new Archon Quest, where a new crisis that threatens to plunge the nation into chaos is brewing. Nahida is out of the picture, and someone who looks suspiciously like Il Dottore has emerged.

If you complete this chapter at launch, you’ll earn up to 560 Primogems, as well as Nicole's Ascension Materials. Nicole is the first of three playable characters arriving with this update. Something else you’ll unlock if you finish the chapter quickly is a new Weekly Boss that HoYo says has “unpredictable abilities.”

And if you haven’t played in a while, don’t worry, you can refer to the Guiding Notes feature to catch you up on what’s been going on in the world. This is part of a larger effort from the team to make story progression more seamless, and also includes improved quest autosave prompts.

Nicole Reeyn is highest-profile and most interesting, being the first playable member of the Hexenzirkel. The mage is a 5-Star Pyro Catalyst wielder intended as a support member of the team. She can boost the ATK of all party members, even those not currently on the field. She also generates a shield while doing so.

Her Elemental Burst allows her to summon an Arcane Projection that follows the active character, sending out Coordinated Attacks that match their Elemental Type. Outside of combat, Nicole can help you find treasures by calling upon a Seelie to guide you to them. Quite fitting, as you’ll be exploring in the inside of the Witch's Lodge in Nicole’s Meeting Point in Luna 7, so bring her along.

Lohen, the Vice Captain of the Knights of Favonius' Fifth Company, is the second new character. Also a 5-Star addition, he is instead a Cryo Polearm wielder designed for aggressive combat. His main use is dealing massive Cryo DMG, and he can do that by managing two resources unique to him: Joy, and Will to Win.

Through his Elemental Skill, he can enter the Masterstroke state, allowing him to build up (and consume) Joy to unleash enhanced skills. The more his teammates fight, the more Will to Win he biulds, which can later be used to boost his effectiveness further. For an even more powerful display of force, bring along a Hexerei character when he’s on your team.

Prune is the third and final addition. Prune is a 4-Star Anemo Catalyst wielder, and her kit is inspired by her Witch Hunter aspirations. Using a bell and a hammer, she can deal DMG of several elements at once, and trigger Swirl reactions.

Nicole, and Lohen will debut in Luna 7’s first half, while Prune will follow in the second. The first half will also see a Durin rerun, with Mavuika returning in the second half. You can look forward to a new limited-time event as part of Luna 7, with a focus on Klee's Little Hexenzirkel.

You’ll find a series of mini-games you can play alongside Prune, as well as Qiqi, Yaoyao, and Sayu. If you play, you could earn the Super Awesome Magic Key, an exclusive weapon skin. Miliastra Wonderland is doing its thing, too, with a new sports festival for you to take part in.

One new gameplay addition worth calling attention to is that Manekins can now perform actions in Teyvat. The Kamera, which you can use to capture moments with Manekins, is getting upgraded, too, with new editing tools and assets.

Before you pick the game back up, be sure to check out our recently-updated Genshin Impact codes page for some free stuff you may be missing.

#4239. Award-Winning Composer And Musician Jon Batiste Talks Ocarina Of Time's Music And Why 'Guile's Theme' Goes With Everything

Jon Batiste has collaborated with the likes of Alicia Keys, Lenny Kravitz, Prince, Stevie Wonder, Willie Nelson, and many more. He performed the national anthem at Super Bowl LIX. He's headed up the musical efforts of The Late Show with Stephen Colbert. He's taken home more awards than we can realistically list in this article (including eight Grammys, as well as an Academy Award, a BAFTA Award, and a Golden Globe). But as I sit down with Batiste for a brief conversation about video game music, his energy transcends the Zoom call.

Before I can even ask a question, Batiste begins singing to greet me, then nerds out about my NBA Jam and Street Fighter II cabinets. He begins humming the menu music from NBA Jam and reminiscing about all the quarters he pumped into his local Street Fighter cabinet. The Louisiana native and Juilliard School alum has been an ardent gaming enthusiast for nearly three decades, with compositions from games like Sonic the Hedgehog and Final Fantasy VII inspiring his earliest musical endeavors. Spend enough time watching video game music performances on social media, and you'll likely soon find videos of Batiste sitting with famed Final Fantasy composer Nobuo Uematsu, or of Batiste performing gaming music.

With The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time delivering some of the most iconic music of all time (and Batiste famously loving the music), it makes sense that Nintendo would bring him out to New York to serve as a special guest at the launch event for the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake on Switch 2. I sat down with Batiste for a few minutes to chat about his love of video game music, his history with Nintendo, and why "Guile's Theme" from Street Fighter II just goes so well with everything.

Ocarina of Time is easily one of the most important video games ever made, and one of the things that makes it so special is the music. What about Ocarina of Time sticks out to you sonically?First off, if you want to get super inside baseball, technical music nerdery, which I love to do, in the compositions, there's a way that major chords and minor chords in... no sevenths, just root, third, fifth. They alternate, and it creates this magic that is, like, it's wistful, and it's simple. It feels ancient, and it feels like it's the music that is going on in your mind as you're generating thoughts and your imagination is churning. And the major chords are happening just after the minors in this contrary motion that's happening, so it feels like the music is going like this: It's going up – major, minor – like [sings the main Legend of Zelda theme song].

So, it's expanding and contracting, which is a musical allegory for the expansion and the openness of the world that Link is in. It's like [Koji Kondo] figured out how to capture the essence of the gameplay, but also the essence of magic and simplicity, which I think is really what makes... that's the music's power! So, you could listen to the music in the game, and you could also listen to it apart from the game and experience that magic.

Are there any tracks in Ocarina of Time that stand out to you as the most musically sophisticated or compositionally impressive?Oh man. Well, I think of it as a suite, so that's what makes it actually... there's nothing that's more or less complex, but the thought to figure out how to make all of the themes be interrelated yet singular. "Song of Storms" is, like, for me, that's a personal favorite. That's why I like to play it. I like to play a lot of the themes. That's how I grew up! I would play the game, and then, I would go to an instrument. Once we played for hours on Nintendo, we'd go and play Nintendo on piano! It was like a trade-off there, you know? I've been doing this since I was about 11 years old.

Taking it back to that 11-year-old Jon, talk to me a little bit about your history in general.Okay, so my history with Nintendo goes back to the NES. Christmas morning. Duck Hunt. You remember that? Maybe the first game I ever played. No, the first game I ever played was Donkey Kong, and then Duck Hunt, and then Super Mario Bros. Staples! We're talking about the early '90s. We had a room where I would go – it was my domain – and we had this blue shag carpet, and I would sit back there, and I would basically disappear into the carpet playing Nintendo for hours and hours.

And my mind is kind of... my mind can become a spiral; it can become a tornado. And I realized even then that going into this world of the game, even if I didn't win – it's not about winning or losing – it helps to organize the spiral of my mind and give me ideas and inspiration. So then, I started to get into Street Fighter II when I started to play more communally with my sister and my cousins. Yoko Shimomura, who I also had the pleasure of meeting and collaborating with, she composed incredible themes for each character, and that's when I really started to get a true love for fighting games.

And then, we would play so many of the Street Fighter franchise. We would play a lot of Final Fight. There were so many things... there was Double Dragon, then we got Mega Man... all these different series. Mega Man X is [an] all-time favorite. And then, here comes The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, and that sort of expands the canon while also blending all of the elements: score, combat, the sort of linear quality of, like, a Donkey Kong or Super Mario World, and expanding the world in that way, expanding the canon in that way. Mind-blowing! So,  that sort of solidified my palate in terms of my favorite type of game.

You mentioned Street Fighter II. There's a meme about "Guile's Theme" and how it goes with everything. #4238. Mystic Messenger's most loyal players are getting banned in droves for seemingly playing the game too much

With the 10th anniversary of Mystic Messenger nearly upon us, the dating sim has inexplicably begun issuing wide-spread bans for its most active players.

Mystic Messenger, arguably one of the best dating sims around, has been dormant for about seven years. Despite not receiving new content or any meaningful updates in all that time, the game remains popular with its core fans, many of whom just woke up to some shocking news about their accounts.

The free-to-play mobile dating sim has started banning players with seemingly too many Hourglasses - the game’s virtual currency - saved up in their accounts. So far, it looks like players with 1,000 or more have been targeted, but others with far fewer hoards have reported getting the axe, too.

The news exploded on the Mystic Messenger subreddit overnight, with over a dozen reports from players logging in to play normally, only to receive an in-game notice that their accounts had been banned.

The message players received is identical, and doesn’t mention the specific reason for the ban. “Your account has been banned because abusive behavior has been detected from your account,” it reads, ending with a support email address the affected user can contact if they believe they’d banned in error.

It didn’t take a while for players to realise that most, if not all of the bans are for players with thousands of Hourglasses in their accounts. The virtual currency can both be acquired in-game just by playing, as well as through direct real-money purchases.

For a nearly ten-year-old game that stopped receiving content three years into its life, it’s easy to see how a dedicated group of players would be able to acquire so many Hourglasses by simply playing regularly for so long.

When contacted by the affected players, Cheritz, the developer and publisher of the game, has instructed them to send receipts of how they acquired Hourglasses (assuming they were purchased) to verify whether or not they’d been fraudulently obtained.

Considering that Mystic Messenger has practically been abandoned by its developer, certain exploits have emerged over the years that allowed players to farm Hourglasses faster than intended, but those instances have always been dealt with then and there.

The blanket and sudden nature of this ban is what’s spooked players, especially those who’ve been logging in for years and never thought accruing in-game currency from playing the game too much would make them the target of a ban.

The running theory is that most of the bans are unintentional, and may be the result of a new automated security system that’s been implemented. It’s entirely possible, especially if its’s AI-based, that the new system simply couldn’t distinguish between those who have earned (or bought) their Hourglasses fairly, and those who used exploits.

The timing of the ban wave is also suspect. With the game’s 10th anniversary coming up in July, it could be that Cheriz is preparing to release a large update for Mystic Messenger, which may include new content. If most of the playerbase is already sitting on massive amounts of in-game currency, they may simply use that to fast-track their way to unlocking the new content, which would greatly affect the developer’s bottom line.

This is a problem that other live service games have run into in the past. Just recently, extraction shooter Arc Raiders added a cap to the amount of Cred players can hold in their accounts very quickly after its launch. That currency is used to buy cosmetic sets in the store, so the logic is easy to follow.

All of that has certainly put a damper on the enthusiasm of the game’s most active players, many of whom were excited to get together in person for the coming 10th anniversary, participate in community nights and so on to celebrate.

It’s also disheartening to see a fanbase so loyal; playing a game as regularly for so long without new content, to be treated so poorly. Even without knowing what the game is, it’s impressive that so many people have kept the flag of their favourite game flying for so long.

Exclusive: The Rings of Power season 3 might be the darkest season yet of the Lord of the Rings prequel

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The Rings of Power season 3 begins at the darkest moment yet for Middle-earth. Sauron is in possession of the Nine Rings for men and is plotting his path to forge the One Ring, all the while sending his Orcs out to conquer new locales.

As a result, the stakes are pretty high for each of the show's beloved characters, and the showrunners reveal that there will be "tragic consequences".

"The elves are clinging on to being able to hold Sauron at bay, but only by the power of their three rings," co-showrunner J.D. Payne tells GamesRadar+. "And Sauron, his plan this season is to be able to neutralize the power of those rings by making One Ring to rule them all. Beyond that, he's also recruiting a massive army by giving out the Nine Rings for men."

As Patrick McKay adds, it's a tense situation to be in and one they wanted to acknowledge with real stakes. "In Lord of the Rings, people turn to the dark side; they fall to evil, and when that happens, there are tragic consequences," he adds. "And we felt that it was important for the audience to feel those viscerally, and for people that you love and whose stories you're excited to watch continue, sometimes the end is not happy for them. That can be painful. But it should be. It shouldn't be fun."

As Payne alludes to, the main frontier against Sauron is the Elves, led by a war-beaten Gil-galad, played by Benjamin Walker. He tells GamesRadar+ that it's not looking great for them when the third season kicks off, either. "It's the little Dutch boy with his finger in the dam, kind of going, 'Everything's fine!' Everything is not fine. If I take my finger out, we're all going to drown. Yeah, it's not great. Outlook is bleak, and the tool, the weapon we have been using are the rings, the power of it is eroding and becoming potentially ominous. So we're in a position where we can't do this on our own."

They look to Númenór, which is facing its own problems of civil war, with Míriel and Pharazôn split across two sides of the conflict. While they're out of the battle with Sauron for now, darkness is on the horizon for the kingdom too, as Míriel star Cynthia Addai-Robinson alludes to.

"There's going to be a lot of heartbreak in this particular part of the world," she explains. "And obviously there is a sense of being duty-bound, there is a sense of sacrifice for the greater good, and they are all driven by this particular worldview, and it just so happens that on the other side of that is Pharazôn and sort of what Númenor has become under his leadership and trying to make sure that it doesn't get to the point of no return. So I might be biased, but I love the Númenor storyline this season, and I think it's doing a very good job of taking us toward the inevitable, if you know where it all goes."

The expanding darkness is felt in all corners of Middle-earth too, as the Dwarven kingdom of Khazad-dûm has shut its doors to try and protect the Dwarven rings. Durin star Owain Arthur explains: "The stakes just keep on getting higher and higher. This is it, and the more power Sauron gets, the more danger there is, the more doom and gloom there is in Middle-earth, but there's hope."

The showrunners were keen to find some levity in this darkness too. This mainly comes from the romantic storyline between Galadriel and her long-lost husband Celeborn, played by franchise newcomer Jamie Campbell Bower. Their reunion is a point of light, which J.D. Payne says was one of their "main objectives this season".

"Romance was an important thing for us this season, and we brought in some writers in our writers' room. We asked specifically, we said, 'We want you to be really hard on us, be really hard on the story, and how do we make this romance work,'" Payne says. "You know, we looked at things that you know in sort of our shared canon of The Princess Bride and Before Sunset, that you know we both love, and you know these stories of what happens when people who loved each other once and have been separated for a long time get back together again. How do you pick the relationship back up?"

The answers will all be revealed when The Rings of Power season 3 begins on Prime Video on November 11. For more on Middle-earth, check out our guide on how to watch the Lord of the Rings movies in order.

#4236. The Video Games And More You Should Play This Weekend – November 6, 2026

This week and weekend is all about the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, one of the few games I feel deserves the title of masterpiece. And the remake is really well done! I got every heart piece, every Gold Skulltala, the Goron Sword, and the biggest pouch for every one of my items over the course of the review... but I am contemplating jumping right back in for another go.

We also revealed our next cover and in case you missed the announcement it is... pause for effect... Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis! It's an awesome cover that celebrates the history of Lara Croft, and along with a cover story on the game, we also have a big retrospective on the series. I highly recommend subscribing to get your issue if you haven't already.

But it wasn't all just Zelda and Tomb Raider this week. Below you will find a list of weekend play recommendations, but before that... some of our biggest stories of the week.

We have been writing a lot about The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time remake this week because it is one of 2026's most exciting games, and it's real good. The remake is not particularly surprising. It mostly sticks to the trajectory of the original game, but there is a reason it is considered one of the best games of all time. It also looks and plays amazing.

You can read the full review here (or watch the video above), but we also have a big interview with the game's producers (one of whom worked on the original Ocarina of Time, and one who directed Breath of the Wild among many other Zelda games), some details about the Easter Eggs that did and did not make it into the remake, and a very handy tip for the game if you happen to be playing with a Switch 2 Pro controller.

World of Warcraft: Forever is out now and it’s a great time to jump into the revamped and expanded version of a project that changed online games forever back in 2004. A thousand new quests, multiple new zones, countless revamps, and an impressively stunning visual overhaul make it the perfect time to jump in for anyone who’s ever been curious to explore Azeroth.

2022's Escape Academy was a sneaky little puzzle game that surprised me and its sequel released this week. Taking place in a school obsessed with puzzles, you play as a student who must make their way through a series of escape rooms. The puzzles are clever, and the setting is charming, but the secret weapon is the local, split-screen co-op. Solving puzzles together is fun especially when one player needs to look at one section of a room to help dictate a solution on the other side of the room. My wife and I both love video games, but rarely play co-op games together just because of our disparate, individual tastes. But Escape Room is one we enjoyed together and we're so far enjoying the sequel. My only complaint so far is... I wish it ran a little better.

While we collectively use the term here for the sake of familiarity, I’m always a bit hesitant in my own mind to label a game under the wide banner of “Metroidvania.” In part, that’s because I think the two referenced games (Metroid and Castlevania: Symphony of the Night) are actually more different than they might appear at first glance. Gloomsoft’s recent release, Moadra, recognizes that distinction, crafting a game that draws heavy inspiration from the specific tradition of Super Metroid, even while presenting an intriguing and atmospheric fiction that is great fun to discover. In movement, actions, and exploration, Moadra feels remarkably similar to  the best of the 2D Metroid games. A scanning tool also leans into the Metroid inspirations, revealing details about the weird alien world you’re navigating. If you’ve been hungry for a game that scratches that particular itch of sci-fi gear/ability-gated exploration, I think you’ll find a lot to love in this game.

I get the Marvel fatigue we've all been experiencing. There are a lot of games and a lot of movies and a lot of TV shows and many are good, but lately most feel like homework. For those reasons, you'd be forgiven for dismissing the 2021 Guardians of the Galaxy game, but I promise you it is good. For one, it is standalone. It does not directly tie to any specific Marvel media. No homework necessary. And for two, it's just a really good game with an affecting story and a unique take on the characters that most of us met for the first time in the movies. And, for the BioWare fans out there mourning the loss of Mass Effect, this game has some Mass Effect energy. It's available on Switch 2 this week and I happily recommend it, especially if you missed it five years ago.

This exclusively two-player board game features a fun mix of activities. You act as both a dungeon architect, and an adventurer delving into said dungeons. Each player creates their own version of a challenging dungeon filled with traps, monsters, and treasures.

But you’re also forced to take on the dangers of your opponent’s crafted dungeon, to see who manages to come out on top. If you have fond memories of the hidden-info nature of old games like Battleship, but you want some greater strategic depth and fantasy flavor thrown in, this one is a great pick.

#4235. Forza Horizon 6 explodes on Steam even before it's officially out

Forza Horizon 6 looks to have easily delivered the most successful launch for any game in the series on PC, with record-breaking player numbers.

Steam is abuzz this week with a couple of long-anticipated launches, but in Forza Horizon 6’s case, at least, the game isn’t even out for what will be most of its players. The anticipated sequel in the open-world driving game series doesn’t officially launch until May 19, but owners of its most expensive version - the Premium Edition - can play it right now.

That version of the game includes more than just a few days of early access, of course, but you’d think the $120 price tag would’ve only been palatable to a small group of players. Not the case with this game.

Forza Horizon 6, which has spent 16 weeks in Steam’s global top sellers list, currently occupies the number two spot, having jumped up three spots this week in anticipation of the launch. The game has also naturally been popular with players, so popular in fact that it has already overtaken the player counts of all other Horizon games on the platform.

At the time of writing, the game has peaked at 128,157 concurrent players on Steam alone (via SteamDB). The figure has already climbed several times during the writing of this story, so you can only imagine how much higher it’s going to get deeper into the weekend.

All of that, of course, days before the official launch on Tuesday, when, theoretically, the majority of the game’s audience will be able to start playing. In just a few short hours, Horizon 6 has already gone well above Forza Horizon 5’s peak concurrent of 81,096, as well as Forza Horizon 4’s peak 75,689 players.

Steam is the only platform that publishes player numbers, of course, but it’s easy to see how similar the enthusiasm is going to be on Xbox. Though the game is not yet part of the Game Pass line-up, those who don’t want to wait could buy the Premium Edition Upgrade to get the included content, and play it right now.

Game Pass, and Xbox / Windows Store numbers don’t factor into Steam’s, which is another thing to consider when viewing the numbers holistically. Indeed, given how successful Forza Horizon 5 has been on PlayStation 5, Horizon 6’s upcoming release on Sony's console is bound to be even bigger.

Forza Horizon 5 has been off to a similarly flying start in the first few days of its own advanced access launch, so it’s obviously not surprising to see Horizon 6 do better there. In case you missed it, check out our review of Forza Horizon 6. In short, we really liked it, even if we expected more.

#4233. Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.3 will take us deeper into the World in Canvas and make Mortenax Blade playable

Honkai: Star Rail's next big outing will see the continuation of the Planarcadia story, and it's going to be with us soon.

HoYoverse has today delivered full details on the next major update for Honkai: Star Rail. Version 4.3, dubbed The Lethe Below the Living, will be available for all players on June 1. The upcoming update adds a new chapter to the Planarcadia arc, and introduce a new playable character.

The new narrative chapter will also unveil more about Mortenax Blade, the Trailblazer themselves, and the husk of the Aeon.

Mortenax Blade is the hero of this chapter, and he’s going to step into the World in Canvas. The goal is to - by borrowing the power of Voracity - excise Shuhu from his body and end the curse.

The Trailblazer goes on a trip of their own in Version 4.3, this time to Inkford Hermitage, right on the edge between the World in Canvas and the real world. They’re going to undertake this journey to warn Graphia of the Asat Pramad threat.

In case you hadn’t already guessed, Mortenax Blade is this version’s new playable character. The 5-Star Fire-Type swordsman is on the Path of Nihility. Blade’s Ultimate allows him to enter an enhanced state by deploying a special Bounded Field.

While the field is active, all enemies receive more DMG. Entering this state is also how Blade unlocks his skill, which uses a Sword Formation to deal more damage. This is then used to essentially unlock a second, more powerful Ultimate for him.

The benefits of Mortenax Blade’s kit extend to his teammates, too. Any ally who attacks an enemy with him on the team, they inflict a debuff on them. This also builds up a special Charge that Blade can later use with his Skill.

Version 4.3’s launch arrives alongside the Gift of Tempered Blade event. Through it, you can claim a new Trailblazer Outfit piece for free, but only after getting Mortenax Blade from Warping. The first phase’s rerun will be Yao Guang, and the second phase will bring back both Cyrene and Phainon.

You can also expect the Wispae Amusement Park to arrive within the World in Canvas, which you’ll get to design. You can plan where the rides will go, pick the different themes, set visitor routes and more.

Starward Mode is another new addition, which can be found in Memory of Chaos, Pure Fiction, and Apocalyptic Shadow. Starward will see you take on three different stages, which you’ll need three teams for. Clearing each challenge with full stars will reward you 100 Stellar Jades extra per chase.

There’s more coming down the line, too. A new Fate/Stay Night [Unlimited Blade Works] collaboration will arrive in a content up this summer. The event will give players a chance to earn Gilgamesh or Archer for free by logging in.

It turns out that it wasn't all makeup and that Matt Damon really was just that exhausted in The Odyssey, as the star reveals he was awake for almost two days straight while filming the movie's most intense scene.

"I had it happen two or three times on this movie where I just didn’t sleep," explains Damon in an interview with GQ. "I was tired and I went to bed, and I’m sure everyone’s had that feeling where you’ve got to get up the next day and you have something that you have to do and you can’t fall asleep and you’re kicking the blanket around and you’re staring at the ceiling. By the time I got to work to do the scene with Samantha [Morton], I hadn’t slept in 24 hours, and by the end of the day it was 36 or whatever."

We assume that Damon is talking about that unforgettable scene in Circe's cabin. After losing many soldiers to the giants of Telepylos, Odysseus' men begin to lose trust in him, so when they reach Circe's island, they split up. But when they stumble upon Circe's hut, she lures them with a magical broth and eventually turns them into squealing pigs. Odysseus goes looking for them and confronts the witch, and in a long and tense conversation, we learn about Circe's dark past and twisted motivations.

Damon says his sleep deprivation actually helped him in this scene, which makes sense, as Odysseus himself wouldn't be that well-rested either after watching his men be torn apart by Laestrygonians and then desperately searching for a new island to dock at before he and his men starve to death. "I remember thinking the great thing about this character is he probably didn’t sleep last night," added Damon. "So the weariness was very real for a lot of the movie."

The whole project was a huge undertaking, though. The Odyssey was shot on location around the world, from remote caves in Greece to open scenes, where Christoper Nolan got through 400 miles of film while shooting on the open sea. But Damon says he is glad he got to do it at this point in his career, adding, "I don’t think I would’ve appreciated it as much 20 years ago," as even though "there was a lot of physical discomfort that was temporary," he "felt so grateful to be there. I was just so joyful the whole time that I didn’t really notice any of that."

For more, check out our ranking of the best Christopher Nolan movies and keep up with all of the new movies heading your way.

#4231. Zelda: Ocarina Of Time's Director Was Chosen For His Ability To "Solve Problems Very Aggressively"

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Switch 2 gained a new director in HokWai Ng, a developer at Nintendo who started his career with Wii Fit Plus before becoming involved with planning on Tears of the Kingdom for the Switch.

In a new interview with Eiji Aonuma and Hidemaro Fujibayashi over on Polygon, Aonuma commented on the reason why Ng was chosen to lead the development on Ocarina of Time. He cited Ng's ability to "solve problems very aggressively, very proactively" during his time on Tears of the Kingdom, while his idea for future projects made Aonuma believe that he would be the right fit for a remake.

"He was involved with the planning on Tears of the Kingdom, and he was someone on that project that I saw find and solve problems very aggressively, very proactively. And so I knew that would be a great opportunity to see him do more. I thought it'd be really interesting to use him on this project. In fact, at the end of Tears of the Kingdom, he started to present some ideas for future projects that made me think, "Okay, yeah, you're interested in something like a remake. I think you've got your own ideas here. Perhaps you should work on this as a director." And this has been a really good experience. I think [it was] a good decision."

It's honestly so lovely to see Nintendo continue to work with younger generations of developers and provide them with such opportunities. It's certainly not something we're used to seeing here in the west, that's for sure.

Needless to say, we think HokWai Ng has done a remarkable job on Ocarina of Time, and we're keen to see what else he might do with the Legend of Zelda franchise in the future.

#4230. Monopoly Go x The Simpsons crossover is almost here

After a long wait and exhaustive leaks, the highly-anticipated Simpsons event will finally arrive in Monopoly Go very soon, alongside new content.

Monopoly Go players have been looking forward to a major crossover event for what felt like months, and though most of the details ended up leaking, nothing actually beats official information.

The world of The Simpsons has officially arrived in Monopoly Go, and there's a whole lot for players to dive into. The show's creative team even produced a new animated short, featuring Mr. Monopoly, and Mr. Burns.

Available June 3 through July 29, the new event allows Monopoly Go players to jump in the world of The Simpsons. You'll be able to build, and explore all around multiple iconic locations from the show.

Along the way, you'll run into Simpsons characters like Homer, Marge, Bart, Lisa, and of course, Mr. Burns. Developer Scopely teamed up with the show's creative team to create many references, and Easter Eggs for you to discover. You'll find some of those on chance cards, but most of the world has been changed to be part of The Simpsons, including getting to bribe Chief Wiggum to escape jail.

The developer promises a deeply connected world with Simpsons narratives and characters that alter seasonal maps, and offer unique sticker sets and animated sequences to dive in. Incidentally, this is The Simpsons' first appearance in a mobile-exclusive game in 13 years.

Here's a breakdown of everything you can expect, straight from Scopely:

Episodes: Narrative-driven encounters that create stories inspired by The Simpsons. Episodes play out across seasonal boards, sticker sets, and minigames, all capped off with an animated short.

Sticker sets: Every Episode comes with its own limited-time sticker set, taking cues from the latest Simpsons story. Collectible artwork, character journeys and other rewards are yours to claim for the duration of each Episode.

The Simpsons Run: Every two weeks, a new Springfield character will take over the Free Parking tile, kicking off character-driven runs.

Simpsons-themed Shutdowns and Heists: Monopoly Go's shutdowns and heists get a Simpsons makeover, with Springfield-inspired chaos and disasters.

Bribe Wiggum: This changes Go to Jail to allow players to bribe Chief Wiggum, giving you a chance to earn a bigger reward, but not without introducing an element of unpredictability.

Simpsons chance cards: The chance card collection grows with over 50 Simpsons-themed cards full of memes, references and one-liners from the show.

If you're excited to jump in tomorrow, be sure to check out these Free Monopoly Go Dice Links before you dive into the new content.

Secret Wars isn't going anywhere (for now)

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Despite some well-meaning discussion around whether Avengers: Secret Wars would make its release date, it appears Disney and Marvel Studios have no intention of a delay.

As documented by Hablemos de Cine, the Argentinian Disney 2027 Upfront event featured confirmation that – for now, at least – Secret Wars remains set for December 17, 2027. The 2028 movies, X-Men, Ghost Rider, and Black Panther 3, are also still locked in.

A direct sequel to Avengers: Doomsday, Secret Wars is set to bring the Multiverse Saga to a close. As of right now, the only confirmed details we have arrived courtesy of San Diego Comic-Con in 2024 – namely, Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom would be joined by the main casts of Thunderbolts and Fantastic Four.

Anthony Mackie also said he will be back as Captain America, but has said he won't be filming Secret Wars until July – hence the whispers that Secret Wars would need to be pushed back into 2028 to accommodate various actors' schedules.

As of late July this year, directors Anthony and Joe Russo were starting to "sweat" with how close they were to beginning Secret Wars filming but, unless everything has been completely under wraps, it appears there hasn't been a great deal of progress made with production this year.

Still, there's the small matter of Avengers: Doomsday to get out the way first. A new synopsis promises an "existential threat" amid the uncertain future of the multiverse.

Early ticket sales are reflective of the excitement around the movie, too, with numbers already crossing $125 million over a month out from release. Maybe Secret Wars can wait a little longer?

#4228. 'A Tired Parent Mode': The Witcher 3 Dev Explains the Point of Remaster's Accessibility Options

One of the biggest additions to The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered is a suite of accessibility options, letting players tweak various aspects of the game in order to tone down its mechanical friction.

When used in conjunction with the game's easier difficulty setting, you can transform Geralt's adventure into a very laid back, story-focused experience.

However, some people view these kinds of accessibility features as little more than cheats under a modern name — but that's far from the intention, according to Remastered's director of player experience Karolina Niewęgłowska.

In a really interesting developer commentary post on CD Projekt Red's official forums, Niewęgłowska provides details on the thinking behind Remastered's accessibility suite — which is dubbed 'Bard's Ballad' as a preset.

"Bard’s Ballad is for those having difficulty concentrating, including those with ADHD, or those experiencing cognitive fatigue, for example due to conditions like depression," she explains.

"But it’s also for folks who simply feel tired or overwhelmed in this busy world. A colleague to whom I described Bard’s Ballad said 'so… a tired parent mode'. Very much so. But it is for anyone who wants to use it, to play in a way that fits their needs best."

In truth, I've never really thought about accessibility options from this kind of perspective. Sometimes players are just knackered, and they just want to enjoy a bit of escapism without having to commit to a challenge.

"If you only have an hour at the end of your busy day, and have little energy left to manage and organise things, it may be the opposite of what you need. And Bard’s Ballad is addressing that," the director continues.

Niewęgłowska also brings up the smaller toggles, and how they can help players who might be struggling with OCD-like impulses — which is fascinating in itself, given how many open world games push you to visit every little map marker and collect every possible resource.

"There are also settings under Bard’s Ballad to turn off showing herbs and corpses on the minimap. Those are normally helpful. But for some people the dots on the minimap are a distraction, calling 'hey, I’m here, do something about me!', or induce uncertainty or fear of missing out: 'do I have to collect them all?'"

"No, you don’t have to, especially if your main motivation is to experience the story and the world. If having fewer signals on the screen can help you enjoy the game in peace and focus, the toggles are there for you."

She concludes: "Another major change that deserves a highlight is the rise of cognitive overload in the modern world. The digital world constantly bombards us with stimuli, and each year there is more. Notifications, ads, feeds, reminders. Never before in history have humans been exposed to as much information daily. And if we consider this context, ways to manage cognitive load become more useful than ever."

I think Niewęgłowska's post ends up being really insightful, so I thought it was worth sharing here. The Witcher 3's over a decade old now, and I reckon anything that can help as many people as possible enjoy such a landmark game deserves praise.

Have you made use of Remastered's accessibility options? Have you struggled with any of the issues that Niewęgłowska brings up? Take it easy in the comments section below.

#4226. 'Pikmin 4 - Switch 2 Edition' Overview Trailer Showcases More Dandori Academy Exams

It's always Ocarina of Time this, Grand Theft Auto VI that. Have we all forgotten about November's biggest release? The one launching one week today, no less?

That's right, Pikmin 4 - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy is on the horizon, and Nintendo has released a new overview trailer to remind us all that it exists showcase some of its fresh features.

Things start off with the new Switch 2 technical features, like the resolution bump to 4K and the chance to shout out commands to Oatchi via the built-in microphone. There are also some Dandori GameShare opportunities inbound, so you can go head-to-head across systems with only one copy of the game.

Moving on to the new game content, we have the bonus Dandori Academy mode. This one is all about testing your treasure hunt strategies to bring items back to the S.S. Beagle as quickly as possible. Six Dandori stages will be released each month, with exams cropping up every weekend for you to prove your skills.

It looks like the Dandori Academy updates will keep coming throughout the next 12 months, with 72 stages being added in total. Performing well in the exams will net you in-game prizes like photo stamps and user icons.

We'll admit that it feels like this Switch 2 Edition is going to be a little swept under the rug this month, but hey, more Pikmin is always good news!

#4225. Keanu Reeves will return as John Wick in an animated prequel about his impossible task

Join the GamesRadar community for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

Keep exploring and earning more as a member.

Get full access to premium articles, exclusive features and a growing list of member rewards.

Keanu Reeves is officially back as John Wick

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Keanu Reeves will officially return as John Wick in an animated prequel film about his infamous Impossible Task.

In the films, it's revealed that Wick pulled off this impossible task in order to win his freedom from the High Table and retire for love. Of course, his wife, Helen, then dies from an illness, leaving behind a gift of a puppy… and you know the rest.

Per Variety, Reeves has closed a deal to return in the film, which will see him on a mission to kill all of his rivals in a single night. Ultraman: Rising director Shannon Tindle will helm the film, with Ryan and Kaz Firpo penning the script. Chad Stahelski, Basil Iwanyk, Erica Lee, and Reeves will produce.

While Reeves is back in animation, then, it seems he'll also be back in live-action, too. Wick died at the end of John Wick 4, but returned for a supporting role in the prequel movie Ballerina, starring Ana de Armas. He'll also be returning for John Wick 5, despite being dead.

"Keanu, Chad [Stahelski], Basil [Iwanyk] and Erica [Lee] would not return unless they had something truly phenomenal and fresh to say with these characters and this world," Lionsgate's motion picture chairman Adam Fogelson said at CinemaCon. Iwanyk and Lee added: "It's so important to get this story right and give John's story the proper next step. It's exciting to take the first step on that road."

Time will tell what John Wick 5 involves, but for now, we can look forward to seeing Reeves back in animation.

While you wait, check out our guide to all the most exciting upcoming movies for the rest of 2026.

#4224. Poll: Is Phantom Blade Zero Too Hard?

Now that Phantom Blade Zero's been out for a good few days, I thought it'd be interesting to check in on how everyone's finding the experience in terms of difficulty.

This has been a constant topic ever since the game was first announced, with onlookers initially questioning whether it would be a hard-as-nails Soulslike.

However, developer S-GAME has continually stressed that Phantom Blade Zero is not in the same category as FromSoftware's punishing action RPGs; it's got difficulty settings, and you don't lose any resources upon death.

Indeed, Phantom Blade Zero is a fairly forgiving game overall — at least in terms of structure. Where it presents a challenge is in mastering its combat, which often demands careful defensive timing and therefore knowledge of your opponent.

Just before launch, I wrote a sort-of-guide on the title's difficulty, which concludes that while Phantom Blade Zero isn't brutally difficult — unless you're playing on the hardest Hellwalker setting — it's still not an 'easy' game to beat.

Feature How Difficult Is Phantom Blade Zero?

A helpful overview of the game's challenge

Guide Phantom Blade Zero: Best Weapons and Where to Find Them

More experienced action game players will likely push through the adventure with relatively few deaths on the easier 'Wayfarer' and standard 'Pathbreaker' options, but others could still struggle to progress at certain points.

With that in mind, I've seen somewhat mixed takes on the game's general level of challenge, even across this site's own comments sections.

As you can probably imagine, some believe that it's actually very manageable — particularly when compared to its perceived peers, while others have expressed frustration with certain combat mechanics and difficulty spikes.

This kind of divide was always going to manifest, I think, but that's why the topic makes for an intriguing poll.

So, what do you think of the difficulty in Phantom Blade Zero? Is it just right? Actually easy? Or maybe way too hard? Vote in our polls, and then explain your stance in the comments section below.

Robert (or Rob if you're lazy) is an assistant editor of Push Square, and has been a fan of PlayStation since the 90s, when Tekken 2 introduced him to the incredible world of video games. He still takes his fighting games seriously, but RPGs are his true passion. The Witcher, Persona, Dragon Quest, Mass Effect, Final Fantasy, Trails, Tales — he's played 'em all. A little too much, some might say.

#4223. Boltgun 2 and Warhammer Survivors devs Auroch Digital say they're laying off 25% of their staff in now-deleted posts

Not long after releasing boomer shooter Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun II and right before Warhammer Survivors launches in November, developers Auroch Digital have unfortunately given a public statement confirming that roughly a quarter of its current staff will be laid off as part of a restructuring. What's strange — to the point that layoffs are, unfortunately, expected — is that the initial social media posts, on both LinkedIn and Twitter, have now been deleted.

In the studio's statement, posted yesterday, Auroch notes their pride in Boltgun II and Starship Troopers: Ultimate Bug War, both released this year, but "despite that creative success, the same market conditions that have challenged so many of our fellow developers have now also affected us." Apologies to the staff affected follow, with a plea "to partners and friends in the industry: if you are hiring, please consider finding a place for our staff in your studio. They have worked on everything from indie shooters to AAA [co-development], and their talent and breadth is second-to-none." The studio also confirms that post-launch development on both Boltgun II and Warhammer Survivors will continue despite the loss of staff.

This is, sadly, not an uncommon thing to report on by any means. There are layoffs every goddamn week, if not several. This is unique, though, in that in the time between the post going up yesterday and my writing of this piece, the public statements have been deleted. There's an archive of the original image posted here, as you won't find it on Auroch's Twitter or LinkedIn anymore. Even with the barrage of layoff news, I can't think of another time that a statement has been outright retracted within a day. Whether this was posted in error, too early, or some other reason I can't know of, hopefully there'll be some clarity soon and, more importantly, opportunities available for the staff affected.

RPS have reached out to Auroch Digital for comment and clarification.

Now that the $55 billion deal seeing EA go private under Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, Silver Lake, and Jared Kushner's Affinity Partners is done and dusted, the former two are reportedly looking to purchase another big name in gaming: Unity.

The EA buyout hasn't been a simple process, to say the least, with the studio facing backlash following the closure of BioWare and cancellation of Mass Effect 5, but it's settled – legally, anyway – nonetheless. As for Unity, news of its own potential move under the PIF and Silver Lake's wing comes directly from Reuters, which claims to learn as much from anonymous "people familiar with the matter." So, what exactly is happening?

Well, according to the report, Unity – also operating as Unity Software Inc. and Unity Technologies or simply Unity – is in talks regarding its acquisition, with Silver Lake and Saudi Arabia's PIF at the forefront. If you're out of the loop on what Unity itself is, it's most well-known for its cross-platform game engine, which powers quite a few notable titles, both AAA and indie. Think everything from Genshin Impact to Among Us.

As for the possible deal, it's important to note that Silver Lake already owns about 8% of Unity. And, as per Reuters, it recently approached the company alongside the PIF in, discussing a valuation of some $25 billion. The parties involved haven't struck any sort of solid deal yet, however, with Unity supposedly working with an investment bank to see all of its options before anything concrete occurs.

It's difficult to tell just what will happen at this point, but I'm certain this will spur a good bit of discussion among developers and users alike. For instance, what could this buyout mean for Unity, should it happen? That remains to be seen – and, sadly, neither Unity, Silver Lake, nor the PIF responded to Reuters' requests for comment, so this is all we're working with in terms of public knowledge about the deal… should it be underway, that is.

"Asking the AI to reproduce a game that has already been made does not make you Kojima," says Unity CEO launching an AI you can use to reproduce games.

#4221. "Mass Effect was my ultimate white whale": Journey composer shares 20 minutes of music created during talks to work on BioWare's recently cancelled RPG

"It's been hard to see dear friends lose their jobs, and this beloved franchise seemingly vanish forever"

The gradual drip of details about and glimpses at what BioWare were looking to cook up with the cancelled Mass Effect 5 continues, this time thanks to a composer who was in talks to come aboard to put together the RPG's soundtrack. Said songsmith, Austin Wintory, has opted to share around 20 minutes of tunes he put together just as an attempt to explore where he might take things if he did end up being hired to score Commander Shepard's next adventure. Naturally, with BioWare's closure, that hasn't come to pass.

The eight tracks in the YouTube video Wintory, whose compositions have graced the likes of Journey and Assassin's Creed Syndicate, has put together range from a main theme, to intense battle tunes, and the sorts of 'ooh, there's something happening' songs that usually accompany key story moments. The opener, dubbed The Legacy of Shepard, blends pensive piano tinkling with bombastic sci-fi swells. The final track's a funkier remixed version of it. I think my favorite might be track seven, Forever Calibrating, just because it's the sort of relaxed and atmospheric backing tune I tend to put on for ambience while working.

"Working on Mass Effect 5 was my career's biggest dream project, my white whale," Wintory wrote in the video's description. "It is my favorite franchise of all time, and for the last couple years I'd been in serious conversations with BioWare and EA to jump in. My suggestion was to treat the original game's masterful Jack Wall/Sam Hulick score as a starting point, and to build on it from there with deeper use of physical, analog synths and a more tightly interwoven use of the orchestra. But a love letter first and foremost (not unlike my approach to the Aliens franchise with Fireteam Elite).

"As part of the ongoing dialogue, I decided last year (2025) to surprise the folks with an elaborate production: nearly 20 minutes of music, fully recorded and produced with synths, vocals and a large orchestra here in LA. I'd not yet learned any narrative details of what they were planning so this was just pure musical exploration. Receiving the news alongside everyone else that EA had decided to not only cancel the project but shutdown BioWare entirely was a deeply felt loss. It's been hard to see dear friends lose their jobs, and this beloved franchise seemingly vanish forever."

The composer closed by thanking BioWare and EA's music department for giving him the chance to put together these experimental Mass Effect tracks.

While this outpouring of info about what BioWare were up to with Mass Effect 5 is likely all we'll ever get of it, given the folks who were working on it have been scattered to the winds, some fans of the series have begun petitioning for Shep's space adventures not to end up rotting in EA's big shed of disused game IP. Though, surprisingly, they appear not to be teaming that call with the assertion that it should ideally be the same devs who were working on the series prior to BioWare's closure that get first dibs on any opportunity to carry on making Mass Effects.

#4220. Poll: Will You Be Using Zelda Notes With Ocarina Of Time?

With the Ocarina of Time Switch 2 remake, Nintendo is once again using its Zelda Notes feature via the Nintendo Switch app for mobile.

While I wasn't able to access and test out the app's features during the review period, I've been dabbling quite a bit since Nintendo pushed it live for launch. And y'know what? It's fine.

Just like Zelda Notes for Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom, there's nothing here that I'd deem essential to the core experience, but if you're after some harmless supplemental material, it does the job.

My favourite feature? Gossip Quests. Provided you've activated Zelda Notes within Ocarina of Time's settings, you can link your phone directly to the software to partake in a little game to hunt down specific locations depicted in photos. Doing so will earn you points, which you can eventually spend on new ocarina songs.

To be clear, these ocarina songs won't unlock anything in-game, but you can access a playable ocarina in the app and learn the songs yourself, tapping and holding the on-screen holes to perform a variety of tunes.

It's surprisingly tricky, and in an amusing turn of events, pressing three holes at once also acted as a screenshot tool for my phone, so I had to go ahead and delete that function in my phone settings.

You can also come up with your own, original songs and share them via QR code. I haven't come up with anything I'd deem even remotely enjoyable for anyone else, but it's a cool little feature. [For the authentic Ocarina experience circa 1998, I need The Simpsons theme, stat! - Ed.]

Once unlocked in the game, you can also view enemies from the Hall of Fallen Foes. The app also provides a wealth of stats, including daily records, and you can also consult maps if you're gunning for 100% completion and test your Ocarina of Time knowledge with quizzes.

Again, it's fine. There are features, like the Gossip Quests, that would have been awesome had they been included in the game itself in some way, and we'd recommend at least giving it a go if you're looking to extend your playtime. (Fingers crossed for a Master Quest update!)
